blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: The innermost `db.add_seat` sits under a `for`, an `if`, a `match`, an `if`, a `for` and two more `if`s, so a reader has to hold seven conditions to know when a seat is added. Three things cost the reader most. (1) `if account.plan != row.plan` (line 18): a newcomer reads it as "only touch accounts whose plan changed" and cannot tell, without the plan, whether skipping new seats on an account whose plan is unchanged is intended — it is the line most likely to be misread; name the rule or explain it in a comment. (2) `seat.contains('@')` (lines 21 and 32) is an unexplained filter repeated twice; give it a name such as `fn is_valid_seat(seat: &str) -> bool` saying what a valid seat is. (3) The seat-adding loop is duplicated between the `Some` and `None` arms (lines 19-26 and 31-36). Flatten with `continue` for an empty email (line 15), and extract a helper such as `fn add_new_seats(db, account_id, existing: &[String], seats: &[String]) -> Result<usize, DbError>` that filters with `is_valid_seat` and skips existing seats, called from both arms. Behavior stays the same.
findings.title: `import` nests five levels deep, duplicates its seat loop and leaves its filters unexplained
